messages:
marie: Heads-up, seeing a weird stochastic IOPS decay on the us-west2-ephemeral pool for the last ~40m. GPU attach failures started spiking ~30m ago. :eyes:
ryan: any correlation with janitor/scrub jobs?
sudha: timeline? were there large batch jobs or a deploy around then?
marie: no user deploys. most churn looks like nightly janitor windows but this started midday. attaching quick iostat from one affected host:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await  r_await  w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         120.5   850.2  2048.0  5120.0  22.3    4.1     24.1    1.8   92.7
```
marie: tail of dmesg shows NVME retry bursts and controller pause events.
```
[ 2300.123456] nvme nvme0: I/O 0x7f8c failed, status: 0x400 - retrying
[ 2300.234567] nvme nvme0: controller thermal event, throttling
```
alex: thermal? fan telemetry for that rack?
marie: temp is normal (42C). SMART shows rising write amplification counters and increased media errors on subset: attr 241/242 beginning ~6 hours ago.
sam: ops-oncall pulled 5 hosts from the pool; were those the ones showing errors?
ops-oncall: I took nodes n-west2-ephem-{12,15,19,20,23} OOB out of rotation and disabled scheduling on them at 1711346145. saw immediate drop in attach failures.
ben: infra-bot alerted on a slow growth in janitor run time earlier today. log snippet: `janitor.cleaner.run_time_ms p50=60 p95=2200 p99=9800`
ryan: that p99 is suspicious — if janitor sweeps a hotstripe it'll spike IO. maybe overlapping janitor + compaction + batch-backfill.
sudha: can we correlate janitor schedules with the SMART bump? any ATIME on writes?
marie: overlay of metrics shows janitor start spikes at 1711342800 and again at 1711345200, right before the big error window.
alex: quick mitigation: throttle janitor concurrency to 1 for us-west2-ephemeral and postpone heavy GC to midnight. can someone flip the flag?
sam: I can patch and roll a config to reduce concurrency and increase inter-job sleep. Will do a small canary on 3 hosts.
marie: we also put a temporary KV-cache bump to reduce write amplification for model caches — helps but not enough.
ops-oncall: after pulling nodes and throttling janitor, attach failures dropped from 12/min to 1/min.
ben: longer-term we should consider QOS on local-ssd iops or migrate ephemeral to NVMe generations with better write endurance for batch jobs. cost impact estimates?
ryan: rough calc: moving 20% of ephemeral capacity to QOS-backed devices increases monthly spend by ~18% but reduces attach-failure downtime risk by a lot.
sudha: also we can change janitor to be locality-aware to avoid sweeping hotstripes while GPU scheduling is high.
marie: filed a quick RFC ticket: https://rwd/infra/ops/EV-2112 (short note + runbook).
alex: one more datapoint — network spikes seen at 1711345100, small BGP flaps in the region causing rebalancing. might have amplified load as requests retried.
marie: summary plan: 1) continue throttled janitor canary (sam) 2) rotate affected drives for nodes OOB (ops-oncall) 3) temporary KV-cache bump (done) 4) schedule long GC/compaction to off-peak and add locality guard (ryan/sudha) 5) evaluate QOS-backed ephemeral tier + cost (ben).
ops-oncall: executing rotation now; will post host list when done.
infra-bot: alert cleared: ephemeral-pool-iops-degradation (was: high attach-fail-rate) at 1711346370.
deploy-bot: FYI — paused scheduled background compactions in us-west2 for 2h to mitigate.
marie: thanks all. follow-ups: infra postmortem if attach rate still >1/min in 24h, else close. :thumbsup:
ryan: noted, I'll own the RFC changes for janitor locality.
sam: canary rolled to 3 hosts at 1711346280, monitoring.
ben: I'll start cost/benefit on QOS devices, ETA EOD tomorrow.
